correctness.rationale: A cut pair identifies a state bijectively and all legal switches are single-cut steps. For n>2s, the strip s≤y−x≤n−s has positive width: if a needed monotone coordinate move exits, a move of the other coordinate toward the target must enter the strip, by feasibility of the endpoint lift. Conversely every path lifts, giving the minimum of the two cyclic-order lift families. For source gaps d and n−d, alternate cuts give complementary admissible path lengths summing to n; targets on one arc can be paired via its exterior gaps, giving at most d on the short arc and n−d−s on the long arc. The T1 witness has distance m=floor(n/2) by two lift pairings (m and n−m), and its two gaps are feasible even at n=2s+1. For T2 write L=n−s−d and α=floor(L/2); the other candidate lengths d+s+2α and 2n−d−s−2α are both at least L. Radius occurs at d=m and diameter at d=s. Each of the n boundary states for n>2s has two moves, all others have four; n=2s gives n/2 isolates and no connected-case metric is claimed. Independently generated partitions as vertex bitmasks modulo complement and toggled a vertex directly; BFS verified counts, connectivity and all eccentricities for n=3 through 13.
residual_risks: Finite computation supplements but does not replace the strip proof; no radius or diameter conclusion for the frozen graph is used.

originality.rationale: The actual claimed contribution is the extremal evaluation in the size-constrained cycle, not cut-pair encoding, transport-optimality, the all-pairs distance formula, or connectivity. Two general token results already cover the latter exactly, and a prior eccentricity theorem is an actual subfamily overlap. The inspected sources do not evaluate the maximum for every d,n,s or give a stronger extremal theorem implying it.
residual_risks: Unindexed hard-core cycle or partition terminology could contain the full extrema. This pass credits exact prior coverage of pairwise distances and the n=3s−2 special case, not priority for transport.

value.rationale: The exact eccentricity describes worst-case reconfiguration effort state by state in a natural constrained districting problem, showing the change between the floor(n/2) regime and a linear long-arc regime. It diagnoses how a minimum-size rule changes global geometry despite leaving transport distances intact for surviving states. Exact radius and diameter are useful consequences; the elementary counts alone would not justify value.
residual_risks: No implications for other hosts, more districts, or mixing times are established.
